To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of DNA mismatch repair (MMRs) facilitates reactivation of plasmids inactivated by cis-platinum.

the mismatch repair (MMR) system recognizes and repairs both mismatched DNA bases and cisplatin DNA damage, and the loss of MMR reduces the efficiency with which the cell can remove cisplatin damage and re-activate a cisplatin-inactivated gene.

MMR-deficient (MMR−/−) cells, lacking either the hMLH1 protein or hMSH, generated two times more luciferase from a cisplatindamaged luciferase gene than their MMRproficient (MMR+/+) counterparts, whereas the MMR+/+ and MMR−/− cells removed Pt from their genome with equal efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of DNA repair, and in particular, the repair of damage induced by the anticancer drug cisplatin.
understanding the mechanisms of action of cisplatin, the most widely used chemotherapeutic drug for the treatment of solid tumours.
the mechanisms of action of anticancer agents and the mechanisms by which cancer cells become resistant to them.

loss of MMR function facilitates the reactivation and expression of a cisplatinum damaged reporter gene, and that this is a contributing factor to the cisplatinum resistance phenotype.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MMR system can detect and remove cisplatin DNA damage from the genome, but that this detection can be circumvented by the cell, which then can repair the damage.

the MMR system is involved in the detection of the cis-platin adducts in DNA, and the removal of the adducts by MMR-deficient cell lines is more effective, thus resulting in less reactivation of the reporter gene.
loss of MMR does not affect the removal of Pt from total cellular DNA, but does facilitate reactivation of a previously inactivated reporter gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MMR system detects the cisplatin-DNA adducts and that loss of MMR function facilitates reactivation of the reporter plasmid.
the MMR system can be considered a cisplatin detector and that loss of MMR function facilitates the reactivation and expression of a cispllatin-damaged gene.
